name.text: Finding the order of symmetry and angle of rotation of a triangular prism

questiontext.text:
The diagram below shows a triangular prism. A dashed line indicates one of its possible axes of rotation.

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid,{ boundingbox:[-7,6,7,-5], axis:false, showCopyright:false }); var axis={#axis_type#}; /* Prism vertices */ var A=[-4,2]; var B=[-6,-2]; var C=[-2,-2]; var D=[2,3]; var E=[0,-1]; var F=[4,-1]; /* Front triangle */ board.create('polygon',[ board.create('point',A,{visible:false}), board.create('point',B,{visible:false}), board.create('point',C,{visible:false}) ],{ fillColor:'#cfe8ff', fillOpacity:0.4, borders:{strokeWidth:2} }); /* Back triangle */ board.create('polygon',[ board.create('point',D,{visible:false}), board.create('point',E,{visible:false}), board.create('point',F,{visible:false}) ],{ fillColor:'#cfe8ff', fillOpacity:0.4, borders:{strokeWidth:2} }); /* Joining edges */ board.create('segment',[A,D]); board.create('segment',[B,E]); board.create('segment',[C,F]); /* Axis */ if(axis==1){ board.create('segment',[[-1,4],[-1,-3]],{ dash:2, strokeWidth:3, strokeColor:'red' }); } else{ board.create('segment',[[-5,0],[3,1]],{ dash:2, strokeWidth:3, strokeColor:'red' }); } [[/jsxgraph]]

{@axis_name@}

(a) Determine the order of rotational symmetry about the highlighted axis.

Order = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the smallest angle of rotation that maps the prism onto itself about this axis.

Angle = [[input:ans2]]° [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

(a) Order of rotational symmetry

The order of rotational symmetry is the number of times a solid matches its original position during one complete turn of \(360^\circ\) about the given axis.

For the axis shown, the prism matches itself {@order_sym@} time(s) in one complete rotation.

Therefore, the order of rotational symmetry is \[ \boxed{{@order_sym@}}. \]

(b) Smallest angle of rotation

The smallest angle of rotation is found by dividing one complete turn by the order of rotational symmetry.

\[ \text{Smallest angle} = \frac{360^\circ}{\text{Order}} = \frac{360^\circ}{{@order_sym@}} = {@angle_rot@}^\circ \]

Therefore, the smallest angle of rotation is \[ \boxed{{@angle_rot@}^\circ}. \]

Why?

A triangular prism has more than one axis of rotational symmetry.

  • The axis passing through the centres of the triangular faces has rotational symmetry of order 3, because the prism looks the same after every rotation of \(120^\circ\).
  • Each axis passing through the centres of a pair of opposite rectangular faces has rotational symmetry of order 2, because the prism looks the same after a rotation of \(180^\circ\).
